Subject: Access controls and support access — follow-up (FinTrust)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand FinTrust's production requirements. Below is a quick recap and the items we committed to follow up on.

Recap (high level):
- PII scope: customer names, email, masked account numbers, limited financial transaction metadata. You confirmed no SSNs in the payloads we would process.
- Retention: target retention window ~12 months for logs and user content; some business records may require longer.
- Logging & audit: need detailed admin event logs, immutable write-once retention for at least 12 months, and export capability for audits.
- Data residency: primary workload in us-east, but a subset of EU customers requires data-at-rest and processing in eu-west.
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege, separation of duties for admin/support, documented break-glass process, and audited support sessions.

Attachments: redwood_security_faq.pdf (security overview)

Next steps / owners:
1) Alex / FinTrust security: confirm final list of PII fields and any special retention requirements (owner: Alex)
2) FinTrust security: share completed security questionnaire (owner: security@fintrust.com)
3) Dev Patel (SE): provide RBAC recommendation, support access playbook (owner: dev_patel)
4) Marissa: schedule a follow-up technical review + demo (owner: marissa_cole)

Proposed timing: are you available next Wednesday 2027-04-08 for a 45-minute technical deep-dive? We can demo access controls in the eu-west and us-east canaries and walk through break-glass and audit logs.

If you prefer, I can also loop in our Privacy lead for any specifics on retention policy mapping.
\Best,

From: Alex Nguyen <alex@fintrust.com>

Date: 2027-04-01T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls and support access — follow-up (FinTrust)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- PII: confirmed — names, emails, masked account numbers (last 4), and transaction metadata. No SSNs or full account numbers in the data we plan to process.
- Retention: default logs and user content are 12 months; our legal team may ask for up to 3 years for certain compliance archives — we'll flag those if they apply. For the demo, assume 12 months.
- Logging: we need admin/audit logs with user id, action, timestamp, origin IP, and affected resource; exportable in CSV/JSON for e-discovery. Immutable storage for audit logs is preferred.
- Data residency: production user data must remain in us-east for US customers. We do have a small subset of EU residents that require eu-west processing and storage.

I've attached the FinTrust_Security_Questionnaire_v4.xlsx — it has our standard checklist; please have your security/SE team fill the relevant sections.

I'm available next Wednesday 2027-04-08 in the afternoon (after 1pm ET). Thanks — Alex

Attachments: FinTrust_Security_Questionnaire_v4.xlsx

Thanks for the recap, Marissa. A few technical notes from the SE perspective — initial RBAC and support-access recommendations:

1) RBAC model:
   - Roles: Owner, Admin (restricted), Engineer (limited infra), App-Operator (can deploy and view logs), Support (can view runtime metadata but not customer plaintext).
   - Principle of least privilege: default deny; grant only necessary perms per route/model.

2) Support access / break-glass:
   - Break-glass should be an auditable JIT flow: engineer requests elevated session, a manager approves, and an ephemeral token (valid for a short window) is issued.
   - All break-glass sessions recorded (session transcript + metadata), hashed and stored in immutable logs.
   - Mandatory two-person approval for cross-region data access (e.g., to view EU-resident data in a support scenario).

3) Logging & retention:
   - Admin events: retain 12 months by default; support export to S3 with WORM (write once, read many) for archive requests.
   - Request/response traces: sample by default, full tracing for flagged incidents — retention configurable per-customer.

4) Data residency:
   - We can pin model endpoints and associated storage to region (us-east / eu-west).
   - For mixed customers, we provide region-aware routing and data separation at the tenancy level.

5) Evidence / audit support:
   - We can provide SOC 2 artifacts, a redacted architecture diagram, and the RBAC policy matrix.

Attachments: support_access_playbook.md (internal playbook + break-glass flow)

If helpful, I can prep a short demo showing an authenticated break-glass flow, ephemeral token creation, and the resulting immutable log entry.

- Dev
